summary: Modular monolith: ASP.NET Core + Self-managed PostgreSQL serving Blazor (ASP.NET Core), hosted on On-premise Linux servers + Docker Compose (your data centre). Estimated $45-190/month (within the $200 budget).

architecture_rationale.text: One deployable with strict internal modules for the internal_tool domain: a 4-engineer team gets clear boundaries without distributed-system overhead; modules can be extracted later if scale demands it. Over-engineering guard: microservices rejected: 4 engineer(s) cannot absorb the operational overhead.

frontend.justification: Web - Blazor (ASP.NET Core): Chosen because team already works in csharp (team.languages); strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; rich client-side interactivity for a internal_tool; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3.

alternatives.why_not: Blazor scores higher on maintainability and fit for the project type (fit 6.1 vs 6.8).
No javascript/typescript in team.languages: ramp-up time and hiring risk. Blazor scores higher on maintainability and security (fit 2.8 vs 6.8).

tradeoffs: Interactive Server mode keeps a SignalR circuit per user
WebAssembly mode has a larger first download

backend.justification: Chosen because team already works in csharp (team.languages); Microsoft.Identity.Web makes Entra ID SSO a configuration task; strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; strong performance (5/5) with priorities.performance=3.

alternatives.why_not: Self-hosting a full BaaS stack on-premise is operationally heavy. ASP.NET Core scores higher on maintainability and reuse of existing systems (fit 4.8 vs 9.6).
No python in team.languages: ramp-up time and hiring risk. ASP.NET Core scores higher on reuse of existing systems and performance (fit 2.9 vs 9.6).
Excluded by hard constraint: deployment_model=on_premise allows only self-hostable components; Serverless functions is a managed/SaaS service.

database.justification: Chosen because relational integrity and transactions for a internal_tool domain; strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=3; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3; strong cost efficiency (4/5) with priorities.cost=3. Managed as Self-managed PostgreSQL (Patroni/pgBackRest): same platform and private network as the application hosting.

alternatives.why_not: Self-managed PostgreSQL scores higher on maintainability and security (fit 5.9 vs 6.6).
SQL Server licensing outside Azure SQL's managed tiers. Self-managed PostgreSQL scores higher on maintainability (fit 5.7 vs 6.6).
Excluded by hard constraint: deployment_model=on_premise allows only self-hostable components; Google BigQuery is a managed/SaaS service.
Excluded by hard constraint: deployment_model=on_premise allows only self-hostable components; Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL is a managed/SaaS service.

tradeoffs: Single-writer primary: write scale beyond one large node needs partitioning/sharding
Vacuum and connection pooling need attention at scale

hosting.choice: On-premise Linux servers + Docker Compose (your data centre)
hosting.justification: Chosen because runs the ASP.NET Core (.NET 10 LTS) container as-is; strong cost efficiency (4/5) with priorities.cost=3; strong performance (4/5) with priorities.performance=3; strong security (4/5) with priorities.security=3.

alternatives.why_not: Over-engineering for 5,000 users (pays off beyond ~200,000); steep learning curve for a intermediate team. On-premise Linux servers + Docker Compose scores higher on cost (fit -1.5 vs 1.7).
Excluded by hard constraint: deployment_model=on_premise allows only self-hostable components; Google Cloud Run is a managed/SaaS service.

tradeoffs: Hardware, patching, backups and DR are your responsibility

supporting.justification: Chosen because runs inside the on-premise network; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=3; SAML/OIDC broker with LDAP federation; strong cost efficiency (4/5) with priorities.cost=3.

alternatives.why_not: Excluded by hard constraint: deployment_model=on_premise allows only self-hostable components; Microsoft Entra ID is a managed/SaaS service.

tradeoffs: Upgrades and HA are your job
